docs.checked.title: Checked by the test suite
docs.checked.body: Every code block in the guide is parsed, checked and type-checked on each release.
hero.title: A language for websites.
hero.sub: A file describes what a page shows — its elements, the state behind them, what happens when the reader acts. The compiler turns it into a static site, a single-page app, a PDF or a slide deck, with the accessibility, search and performance work done for you.
hero.nodeps: No Node, no bundler, no config
ideas.title: Everything else follows from these
idea.1.title: A file is a list of declarations
idea.1.body: Eleven kinds: `page`, `component`, `store`, `theme`, `app`, `type`, `enum`, `const`, `data`, `animation`, `test`. Pages own their routes; there is no separate route table.
idea.2.title: An element is a typed call
idea.2.body: One positional argument, named props, flags, then a block. The compiler knows every built-in, so a misspelling is an error with a hint — never a silent no-op.
idea.3.title: State is a signal
idea.3.body: `state count = 0` — anything that reads it follows it. Derived values recompute, effects re-run, the DOM updates. No dependency arrays.
idea.4.title: Styles are CSS, written where the element is
idea.4.body: Raw values, design tokens with `$`, nested rules as CSS nesting spells them. One sheet, pruned to what you used.
idea.5.title: The build is the whole site
idea.5.body: HTML pre-rendered per page, a small runtime, a sitemap, Open Graph tags, content-security headers — from `wf build`, with nothing to configure.
ideas.react.title: Coming from React, Vue or Svelte?
ideas.react.body: Skim chapters 2 and 4, then read 5, 8 and 9. The reactivity model is signals, the components are declared and typed, and the compiler checks what you write against what they declare.
outputs.title: One source, four things to ship
output.spa.title: Single-page app
output.spa.body: One `index.html` plus a router that paints pages in the browser. One chunk per page, fetched when its route first shows.
output.static.title: Static site
output.static.body: One pre-rendered HTML file per route, hydrated by the same script. Sitemap, robots and `.gz` copies beside every text file.
output.pdf.title: PDF document
output.pdf.body: A page holds a `Document` with headers, footers, sections and page breaks. A4 or Letter, margins in points.
output.slides.title: Slide deck
output.slides.body: A `Presentation` of `Slide`s, written like any other page, rendered one slide per PDF page.
layouts.title: Braces or indentation — your call
layouts.body: Both compile to the same output, are read by every tool, and a project may mix them. `wf fmt --to wfx` converts a project one way and `--to wf` the other, losslessly.
build.title: Nothing in build/ is hand-edited
build.body: It is regenerated on every build: the page pre-rendered, one directory per route, each page in its own chunk, and a shared sheet carrying your tokens, the built-ins you reached and your stylesheets.
build.point1: A strict content-security policy, satisfied by the output
build.point2: Open Graph, Twitter cards and JSON-LD from each page's title
build.point3: Pre-compressed copies a host can serve as-is
cta.title: Install it and read chapter one
cta.body: `wf init hello` writes a small application — a dashboard, a task list, a settings page, a store, a theme — so you have something to read.
footer.built: Every code block in the guide is real WebFluent 3, parsed and type-checked by the test suite.
notfound.title: Nothing lives here
notfound.body: The address you followed does not match any page. The guide's first chapter is a good place to start again.
search.label: Search the guide
ref.intro: {count} built-in elements in eleven groups, each with its signature, its props, its flags, its events and its parts — read from the compiler's registry, so what this page lists is exactly what the checker accepts. Every element is written `Name(positional, prop: value).flag { block }`.
ref.noprops: This element takes no props of its own.
ref.attrs: Attribute families: `{families}`. Plus the universal props on every element: `animate:`, `exit:`, `speed:`, `class:`, `ref:`.
ref.flags.body: A flag is written after the parentheses with a dot: a `Bool` prop, or a case of one of the element's enum props. A case the enum lacks is an error with a hint.
ref.events.body: Every element accepts these in an `on … { }` handler; an element's own events come first.
ref.generated.title: Generated, not written
ref.generated.body: This page comes from the compiler's registry. Edit the registry, not the page — a prop added there shows up here on the next release.
ref.universal.title: On every element
ref.universal.body: Every element takes these props, and the HTML attribute families named on it (`aria-*`, `data-*`, and the global attributes such as `id`, `class`, `title`, `role`, `tabindex`).
ref.icons.body: The names Icon(…), IconButton(icon:) and Sidebar.Item(icon:) draw; any other name shows as the word, and the compiler warns.
